items.title: Trump declares Iran war 'winding down' in primetime address

featured_image.name: Trump Reportedly Set to Tell Americans Iran War is 'Winding Down ...

items.description:
President Trump delivered a primetime national address on Wednesday evening, telling Americans that the U.S.-Israeli war against Iran is "winding down" and that all military objectives have been met — 33 days after Operation Epic Fury began on February 28.[1][2]

The speech, broadcast from the White House at 9 p.m. ET, capped a day in which Trump escalated his rhetoric on multiple fronts, claiming on Truth Social that Iran's president had requested a ceasefire, threatening NATO allies over the Strait of Hormuz, and telling Reuters in an interview that the U.S. would be "out of Iran pretty quickly" but could return for "spot hits" if necessary.[3][4]

items.title: Iran now charging yuan and crypto tolls in Strait of Hormuz

featured_image.name: Iranian parliament committee approves Strait of Hormuz toll ...

items.description:
Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps has transformed the world's most critical oil chokepoint into what shipping experts are calling a "de facto toll booth," formalizing a system in which vessels must pay fees and submit to vetting for safe passage through the Strait of Hormuz. The development, confirmed by Bloomberg on Wednesday, shows the toll regime now extends to payments in Chinese yuan or stablecoins, with oil tankers facing a starting price of roughly $1 per barrel.[1]

The IRGC-controlled process requires ships to contact intermediaries linked to the paramilitary force. Vessels must submit manifests, crew details, and destination information for what Lloyd's List Intelligence describes as "sanctions screening, cargo alignment checks" and "geopolitical vetting". Approved vessels receive a permit code and are escorted by an IRGC vessel along a northern route around Larak Island, closer to Iran's coastline, rather than the conventional central shipping lanes. Informal tolls of up to $2 million per voyage have been reported.[2][3][4][5]

items.title: Iran's Pezeshkian tells Americans his country 'harbors no enmity' toward them

featured_image.name: Iran sends first significant message of de-escalation, but with ... - CNN

items.description:
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian on Wednesday released an open letter addressed to the American people, declaring that Iran "harbors no enmity" toward ordinary Americans and arguing that portraying Iran as a threat was "neither consistent with historical reality nor with present-day observable facts," according to Reuters and Iran's state-run Press TV.[1][2]

The letter represents a direct diplomatic appeal to the U.S. public amid an ongoing military conflict between the United States, Israel, and Iran that began on February 28 and is now in its fifth week.[3][4]
